fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Israel made Joseph a robe of many colors, and the text gives the reason: Joseph had been born to him in his old age. A rainbow robe? That's my kind of outfit, though I'd get flour on it in about four seconds. (Genesis 37:3)

Twenty shekels of silver, you've got it, friend. The brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt. Twenty shekels, for a brother the text calls their own flesh. I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story. (Genesis 37:27-28)

Hold on, baker, there's no wind in this dream! Not a breeze, not a gust, nothing goes flying. Joseph says the sheaves “…gathered around and bowed down to mine.” It's a field of grain with very good manners, and his brothers did NOT enjoy hearing about it. (Genesis 37:7-8)
